questions.q: Under which treaty was Kashmir sold to Gulab Singh Dogra?
questions.qPa: ਕਿਹੜੀ ਸੰਧੀ ਤਹਿਤ ਕਸ਼ਮੀਰ ਗੁਲਾਬ ਸਿੰਘ ਡੋਗਰਾ ਨੂੰ ਵੇਚਿਆ ਗਿਆ ਸੀ?
questions.explanation: According to the Treaty of Lahore (March 1846), Kashmir was sold to Gulab Singh to pay the war indemnity demanded by the British.

questions.q: Which Sikh general fought to the death at the Battle of Sobraon in 1846?
questions.explanation: General Sham Singh Attariwala fought valiantly and achieved martyrdom at the Battle of Sobraon.

questions.q: Which treaty resulted in the establishment of a British Resident in Lahore and the removal of Maharani Jindan's powers?
questions.qPa: ਕਿਸ ਸੰਧੀ ਦੇ ਸਿੱਟੇ ਵਜੋਂ ਲਾਹੌਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਇੱਕ ਬ੍ਰਿਟਿਸ਼ ਰੈਜ਼ੀਡੈਂਟ ਸਥਾਪਤ ਕੀਤਾ ਗਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਮਹਾਰਾਣੀ ਜਿੰਦਾਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਸ਼ਕਤੀਆਂ ਖੋਹ ਲਈਆਂ ਗਈਆਂ?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Bhairowal (Dec 1846) established a Council of Regency headed by a British Resident.

questions.q: Which battle of the Second Anglo-Sikh War is famously known as the 'Battle of Guns'?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Gujrat (1849) is known as the Battle of Guns due to the heavy and decisive use of artillery by the British.

questions.q: Who was the Governor-General of India when Punjab was annexed?
questions.qPa: ਜਦੋਂ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਨੂੰ ਬ੍ਰਿਟਿਸ਼ ਸਾਮਰਾਜ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਿਲਾਇਆ ਗਿਆ, ਉਸ ਸਮੇਂ ਭਾਰਤ ਦਾ ਗਵਰਨਰ-ਜਨਰਲ ਕੌਣ ਸੀ?
questions.explanation: Lord Dalhousie was the Governor-General who formally annexed Punjab on March 29, 1849.

questions.q: In which battle of the Second Anglo-Sikh War did the British suffer extremely heavy casualties, making it practically a Sikh victory?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Chillianwala was fiercely fought, and the Sikhs inflicted severe damage on the British forces.

questions.q: Who was the British Resident appointed in Lahore after the Treaty of Bhairowal?
questions.explanation: Henry Lawrence was appointed as the first British Resident in Lahore.

questions.q: What was the exact date of the annexation of Punjab by the British?
questions.explanation: Punjab was formally annexed into the British Empire on 29 March 1849.
